claims.statement: A rematch between Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher was expected once calm was restored.
Tom Allen sent a card to a morning paper challenging Mike McCoole to fight for $2,500, within three months and within fifty miles of St. Louis.
Carroll, who kept a dramatic saloon near the Varieties, was understood to have been the go-between through whom Tom Allen and Mike McCoole arranged their match.
Tom Allen wrote to Billy Harding of the New York News challenging Joe Coburn to fight for $2,500 a side or more, in Canada within fifty miles of Detroit, with no excursion and twenty men per party.

Tom Allen wrote to a friend in New York offering to fight Jem Mace a stand-up fight under the new London prize ring rules, two to four months from signing, for $2,000 to $5,000 a side, in Kansas, New Orleans or Canada.
Jem Mace replied from London, through a New York sporting man, that if Allen meant business he would return to America and make the match.

If Mace would not agree, Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn at the same places, wagering $2,500 to Coburn's $1,500, or to fight Ben Hogan for $1,000 to $5,000 with as much training time as Hogan wanted.
Allen offered to fight any man in the world for a stake printed as $1,009 to 35,000 (probably $1,000 to $5,000).
The paper said Joe Coburn was ill and had promised his wife he would not fight again, so a match between him and Allen was abandoned.
Tom Allen had repeatedly challenged Joe Coburn, and would sooner fight Coburn than any man living, according to the Republican.
Tom Allen wrote an acceptance of Jem Mace's challenge.
Allen sent his acceptance to Bell's Life in London for publication, but the paper did not publish it.

Tom Allen said he would promptly accept any challenge from Joe Goss or anybody else to fight for money, for as big stakes as desired, and dismissed a Philadelphia report that Goss had come to challenge him.
Tom Allen said he had given Joe Coburn every chance to fight him, but Coburn would not fight.
Jem Mace wrote to Joe Coburn that Joe Goss, then in New York, had come over on a special mission to fight Allen.
Tom Allen was prepared to fight Joe Goss for any amount Allen named, within twelve weeks of May 2, 1876.
Tom Allen expected to make a satisfactory match with Goss, to be fought in the Southwest.
The fight was to take place four months after articles were signed.
A fight between Tom Allen and Joe Goss, the English champion, was pending in May 1876.
Arthur Chambers and Billy Edwards thought that, if the fight came off, Goss might put it off for at least four months.
Tom Allen had wordy contests with Coburn, Rooke, O'Baldwin and others, which made them his enemies.
Tom Allen wants to fight Johnny Dwyer, who holds the heavyweight championship of America.
Tom Allen planned to challenge any man in the world to fight him for any sum and the championship once his backer had set him up in business.
Tom Allen planned that any fight he made would be held in the Indian Nation on the M., K. & T. road, a day's ride from St. Louis, to avoid police interference.
Tom Allen said he would meet Sullivan, but Sullivan would not meet him.
Tom Allen's backer dropped the match when he saw how puffy and old Allen had become.
A well-known man in the business said Tom Allen put up the first $250 forfeit for the Daly-McManus match.
Tom Allen made the later forfeit deposits himself when the other parties did not come forward, until he had put up the whole $1,000.
Dan Daly said McManus bluffed and challenged him in the theatres and got Tom Allen mixed up in the match.
Dan Daly said Tom Allen and Hugh McManus were both sorry after they got into the match and then tried to get out of it.
It is said Tom Allen stuck on technicalities to avoid the choice of fighting or forfeiting his $1,000.
Ben Hogan (printed as 'tien Hogan') was matched against Tom Allen in a scheme arranged to rob Allen and his backers, carried out by a crowd of toughs.
A representative of 'Dutch' Niel said Tom Allen would back Niel against Johnnie Daly in a skin-tight glove finish contest at 149 pounds for $500 a side.
Tom Allen challenged John L. Sullivan to a fight in New York; the challenge came to nothing.
Tom Allen sought a match with Joe Goss for the championship of America and a $2,000 side bet.
Hogan's backers offered to back him for any amount against Allen, but Allen ignored the challenge.
Ben Hogan challenged Tom Allen for a $2,000 side bet and the heavyweight championship of America, and Allen accepted.
After Allen's poor showing (printed as 'snowing') in the exhibition, Richard K. Fox dropped the idea of Allen fighting John L. Sullivan.
Rooke challenged Tom Allen in the New York papers.
Tom Allen authorized Arthur Chambers to cover the deposit for the Rooke match.
Tom Allen left England to come to America to meet John L. Sullivan.
Hogan challenged Tom Allen to a fight, but Allen said Hogan never intended to fight him.
After the McCool fight, a rematch was negotiated, but McCool withdrew, leaving Tom Allen in actual possession of the title.
Tom Allen had a standing challenge out, offering to fight any man in the world.
A match between Joe Goss and Tom Allen for $2,000 a side had not yet been made.
The headline calls Tom Allen 'the Champion' and says he challenged Joe Goss to fight in the Indian Territory.
Joe Goss said Tom Allen had written him several letters inviting him to come to America.
The postponed McCoole-Allen battle was to come off in about two months.

Joe Coburn offered to back Mike McCoole against Tom Allen in a 24-foot prize ring under the latest London rules, for $5,000 to $10,000, anywhere in the United States, to be fought within sixty days of signing.
Ben Hogan arrived in St. Louis, where he said he came to fight Tom Allen.
After the Gallagher fight, Allen was expected to meet Ned O'Baldwin, then Ben Hogan.
A meeting between Joe Goss of England and Allen, to settle old scores, was expected to take place.
Mike McCoole challenged Tom Allen to a fight, but McCoole's friends and backers prevented the match.
At the Davis fight, Allen wanted to fight Gallagher in the same ring straight after, but his friends prevented it.
At ringside at the Davis fight, Gallagher said he could lick any Englishman in Allen's corner.
After losing to Gallagher by a chance blow, Tom Allen challenged him again.
The proposed fight with Joe Coburn was for $10,000 and was to take place within 90 days, 690 miles west of Omaha.
The fight was to take place fifty miles from Cincinnati or fifty miles from Detroit, which would take it into Canada.
A prize fight between Tom Allen and Jem Mace was anticipated in sporting circles in St. Louis.
The proposed fight with Mace was for $2,500 a side, in Louisiana or Canada, within six months.
